Required Other language third-party pack: JUnit Jupiter (JUnit 5) as a test-scoped dependency via Maven
Maven Surefire Plugin version that supports JUnit 5 (e.g., >=2.22.0)
Logic Analysis: pom.xml

dependency/build; Maven descriptor enforcing Java 11 source/target, adds org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter as test dependency, configures Maven Surefire to run JUnit 5, no external non-test dependencies.
src/main/java/Main.java

runtime/bootstrap; environment-dependent console entry. Builds a deterministic SequenceSpawner (defaultSequence), constructs Board and Game, calls reset(), performs one move, prints grid/score/status, exits. No GUI.
src/main/java/Direction.java
pure-rule; enum of movement directions LEFT, RIGHT, UP, DOWN used by Board.move and Game.move.
src/main/java/MoveResult.java
pure-rule; immutable move outcome holder with exact accessors boolean changed() and int scoreGained(). Constructed by Board.move, consumed by Game.move.
src/main/java/Board.java

domain-entity; sole owner of authoritative 4x4 int grid. Provides deep snapshot via getGridCopy(), exact mutation API setCell(row,col,value) with bounds and 0-or-power-of-two validation. Implements move(Direction) per-line: read 4, compact nonzeros, merge adjacent equal once, compact/fill to 4, write back, sum merged values as scoreGained. Supplies hasTileAtLeast(value), hasAnyMoves(), clear().
src/main/java/Spawn.java
domain-entity; immutable triple (row,col,value). Validates row/col bounds [0..3] and value as positive power-of-two. Consumed by Game via Board.setCell.
src/main/java/Spawner.java
interface; boundary for deterministic spawn source. Declares nextSpawn() -> Spawn. Game consumes exactly two during reset and one after each changed move.
src/main/java/SequenceSpawner.java
domain-entity; deterministic spawner consuming a documented List<Spawn> in strict order; maintains index and wraps by continuing in order. Provides static defaultSequence() used by Main.
src/main/java/GameStatus.java
pure-rule; enum of statuses IN_PROGRESS, WON, LOST. Game updates this after every move attempt, including unchanged moves.
src/main/java/Game.java

orchestration; holds Board, Spawner, score, and status. reset(): clear Board and apply exactly two spawns via Board.setCell. move(Direction): call Board.move once, add scoreGained, if changed then spawn exactly one tile via Board.setCell, then set status: WON iff Board.hasTileAtLeast(2048), else LOST iff !Board.hasAnyMoves(), else IN_PROGRESS. Proxies getScore(), getStatus(), getGridCopy().
src/test/java/MainTest.java
automated-test; single protocol-level JUnit Jupiter test covering deterministic wiring, representative core rules: line merge and score accumulation, spawn-on-change, and status transitions.
Test Scope Plan: basic runtime wiring: SequenceSpawner.defaultSequence() + Board + Game.reset() result determinism and Main runs without IO beyond console.
one small core rule: Board.move single-line merge correctness (e.g., [2,2,0,0] LEFT -> [4,0,0,0]) and score accumulation; also verify spawn occurs only when changed()==true.

headless_testing_risks: Console output only; tests should not assert on stdout to avoid brittleness. Focus tests on core classes.

Shared Knowledge: Protocol files: pom.xml, src/main/java/Main.java (entry), and src/test/java/MainTest.java (single test) are preserved exactly. Java 11, Maven build, JUnit 5 via Surefire. All Java classes are in the default package (no package declarations). Core domain modules are Direction, MoveResult, Board, Spawn, Spawner, SequenceSpawner, GameStatus, Game. Environment-dependent module: Main only. Board exclusively owns the grid; getGridCopy() returns a deep snapshot; setCell() enforces bounds and 0-or-power-of-two validation. Game.reset() applies exactly two spawns; Game.move() spawns exactly once only when the move changed the board; status updated after every move attempt. Tests import Main, Game, Board, Direction, MoveResult, Spawn, Spawner, SequenceSpawner, GameStatus and focus on deterministic wiring and a small core rule.
Execution Protocol: Run mvn -q test. Exactly one protocol-level test file: src/test/java/MainTest.java. No manual interaction or GUI; deterministic, headless console demo via Main. Tests should avoid relying on console output; they should exercise core logic through public APIs. The runtime entry is src/main/java/Main.java.
